subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — p95/p99 latency (hosted vs current provider)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma@finlytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — p95/p99 latency (hosted vs current provider)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Emma — good call. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned on the perf questions: 

Call recap (short):
- FinLytics' primary concern: consistent end-to-end latency at high concurrency for live scoring (financial chat+analytics).
- Key metrics you asked us to qualify: p95 and p99 end-to-end latency, throughput targets (qps), concurrency, and streaming/partial-token requirements.

As discussed, could you confirm the following from your side so we can size the benchmark and test plan?
1) Current provider observed end-to-end numbers (p95/p99) for your typical request profile (see below).
2) Typical request characteristics: average token input, response token count, model(s) in use.
3) Peak concurrency & sustained throughput target (qps).
4) Any strict streaming/partial-token behavior or ordering requirements (e.g., token-at-a-time UI streaming).

FinLytics typical request profile (from call):
- Input tokens: ~300–700 (median ~512).
- Output tokens: ~150–500 (median ~300).
- Model pair: open-model-v2 (approx GPT-3.5-equivalent) via current provider.

Our ask/next steps:
- If you can reply with the current provider p95/p99 numbers and any logs/CSV export, we’ll produce a short SLO comparison (hosted vs. what you’re seeing) and propose a 1-hour benchmark plan using a Redwood test key.
- If acceptable, we’ll schedule a 60–90 minute run with engineering (Rishi/Neha) next week to execute the benchmark.

I’ll draft a proposed target for discussion: hosted API target we aim to demonstrate for your profile — p95 <= 120ms; p99 <= 250ms (end-to-end, same model/config) — but we’ll validate this against your payloads and streaming needs.

Thanks — I’ve attached a short SLO comparison doc we’ll fill after your numbers.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachment: slo-comparison-redwood-hosted.pdf (stub)

From: Emma Carter <emma@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: FinLytics Solutions <solutions@finlytics.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — p95/p99 latency (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers below and I attached a CSV export of our recent production latencies.

Current provider observed (end-to-end, includes network + model inference + app-side processing):
- p50: 180 ms
- p95: 350 ms
- p99: 820 ms
Notes: numbers are for typical conversational scoring calls (input ~512 tokens / output ~300 tokens). We see tail variability during peak trading hours; p99 spikes up to ~1.2s on some days.

Throughput/concurrency:
- Sustained throughput: ~120 qps during business hours
- Peak concurrency: bursts to ~300 concurrent requests for short windows (a few minutes)

Streaming: we do stream partial tokens to the UI for live updates; ordering must be preserved, and we rely on low-latency first-bytes (we can tolerate some streaming chunk delays but not >150ms chunk latency).

Attached: finlytics-current-slo.csv (latency samples for last 7 days) and a small sample request payload set.

We’re also interested to see how Redwood’s hosted API compares for the same payloads — feel free to propose a test plan.

Thanks,
Emma
VP, Product 
FinLytics
Attachment: finlytics-current-slo.csv (stub); finlytics-sample-requests.json (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma@finlytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — p95/p99 latency (hosted vs current provider)

Great — this is exactly what we needed, thanks. A few clarifying points and our proposed plan: 

Clarifying questions:
- The p99 variability to ~1.2s — is that correlated with specific request sizes or times (do you see more tail during >700-token inputs)?
- When streaming to the UI, are you doing server-sent events / chunked HTTP, or a websocket-based stream? Any proxy/load-balancer in front that may buffer?

Proposed Redwood test targets & acceptance criteria (for the benchmark run):
- Redwood hosted API goal for your profile: p95 <= 120 ms; p99 <= 250 ms (end-to-end, including network).
- Throughput target for the run: sustain 150 qps for 20 minutes, then ramp to bursts of 300 concurrent for 5-minute windows to validate tails.
- Streaming goal: initial token latency < 100 ms and chunk latencies < 150 ms for streamed responses.

Plan & next steps:
1) You provide the sample payloads + confirm streaming mechanics (we saw the sample file — thanks).
2) We provide a Redwood test key and a simple harness (script) that replays your requests at target qps/concurrency and captures end-to-end timings.
3) Execute a 1-hour benchmark with Neha and Rishi observing, then share raw logs and a summarized SLO report.

If that sounds good, can you confirm availability for a 60–90 minute run next Wednesday (2026-06-24) or Thursday (2026-06-25)? We’ll block time for Rishi and Neha.

—
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Emma Carter <emma@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: FinLytics Solutions <solutions@finlytics.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — p95/p99 latency (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Marissa — thanks, all sounds good. Quick answers:
- Tail is correlated to request size and also to our in-house pre-processing stage which can add variance; we’ll attach a note about the heavy requests.
- We stream via chunked HTTP through a proxy (Nginx) — it generally passes chunks through but can buffer if upstream latency spikes; we’ll include the proxy config.

We’re available for the benchmark on Thursday 2026-06-25 10:00–11:30am ET. I’ve CC’d Priya (engineering lead) who’ll join the run and owns the sample payloads.

Next steps on our side: we attached the sample payloads and a short README for the pre-processor. We’ll also upload the proxy config to the Drive link in the thread.

Please send the Redwood test key and harness script when ready and we’ll run the replay. If the preliminary results look promising we’ll expand the test to an on-prem ded cap later in the cycle.

HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/FinLytics

Thanks — speak Thursday,
Emma
VP, Product | FinLytics
